1984.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
1984.author: George Orwell
1984.summary: A dystopian novel set in the totalitarian superstate of Oceania, following Winston Smith, a low-ranking Party member who secretly harbors rebellious thoughts against the regime of Big Brother. The novel explores themes of mass surveillance, psychological manipulation, historical revisionism, and the destruction of individual autonomy. Winston begins a forbidden love affair with Julia and makes contact with what he believes is an underground resistance, culminating in his capture, torture, and psychological dissolution by the Thought Police.

harry potter philosopher's stone.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
harry potter philosopher's stone.author: J.K. Rowling
harry potter philosopher's stone.summary: The first novel in the Harry Potter series. Harry Potter, an orphan raised by his neglectful aunt and uncle, discovers on his eleventh birthday that he is a wizard. He enrolls at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, where he befriends Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger and learns about his famous past — his parents were killed by the dark wizard Voldemort, who was defeated when his killing curse rebounded from infant Harry. The story culminates in Harry preventing Voldemort from obtaining the Philosopher's Stone and returning to physical form.

the kite runner.title: The Kite Runner
the kite runner.author: Khaled Hosseini
the kite runner.summary: Set in Afghanistan, the novel follows Amir, a privileged Pashtun boy from Kabul, and his complex relationship with Hassan, the son of his father's Hazara servant. After witnessing Hassan's assault and failing to intervene, Amir is consumed by guilt. The Soviet invasion forces Amir and his father to flee to California. Years later, Amir returns to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan to rescue Hassan's son, seeking redemption for his childhood cowardice.

voices from the margin.title: Voices from the Margin: Rural Narratives in Post-War Fiction
voices from the margin.author: Dr. E. Hartley
voices from the margin.summary: An academic study examining how rural and working-class voices are represented — and systematically marginalized — in post-war British and American fiction. Hartley argues that canonical literary criticism has privileged urban, middle-class perspectives, and recovers a counter-tradition of rural modernism. The book draws on archival materials, oral histories, and close readings of neglected texts to reconstruct a literary geography of the postwar margins.

project hail mary.title: Project Hail Mary
project hail mary.author: Andy Weir
project hail mary.summary: A science fiction novel in which Ryland Grace, a lone astronaut, wakes from a coma aboard a spacecraft with no memory of his mission. He gradually recalls that he is humanity's last hope: sent on a suicide mission to investigate a microorganism called Astrophage that is dimming the sun and threatening Earth's extinction. In deep space, Grace encounters Rocky, an alien from the Eridian system facing the same crisis, and the two form an unlikely partnership across the language barrier to solve the problem together.

babel.title: Babel, or the Necessity of Violence: An Arcane History of the Oxford Translators' Revolution
babel.author: R.F. Kuang
babel.summary: A dark academic fantasy set in an alternate 1830s Oxford, following Robin Swift, a young Chinese scholar brought to England to study translation at the Royal Institute of Translation — known as Babel. The novel explores how the empire's magic system, powered by silver bars engraved with matched-pair translations, depends on the loss of meaning between languages, which in turn depends on colonized peoples. As Robin grows disillusioned with Oxford's role in British imperialism, he is drawn into a revolutionary movement.
babel.note: This is a metadata summary only. Full text not included.

madame bovary.title: Madame Bovary
madame bovary.author: Gustave Flaubert
madame bovary.publisher: Revue de Paris (original); Penguin Classics (modern ed.)
madame bovary.summary: A realist novel following Emma Bovary, a doctor's wife in provincial Normandy who, bored with her marriage and everyday life, pursues romantic affairs and accumulates debt in search of the passionate life she imagined from novels. The novel is celebrated for Flaubert's mastery of free indirect discourse, rendering Emma's romantic illusions from within while maintaining ironic distance. Published in the public domain.
madame bovary.note: This is a metadata summary only. Full text not included.

molecular biology of the cell.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell (7th edition)
molecular biology of the cell.author: Bruce Alberts, Rebecca Heald, Alexander Johnson, David Morgan, Martin Raff, Keith Roberts, Peter Walter
molecular biology of the cell.summary: The standard graduate-level textbook in cell and molecular biology, covering cell chemistry and bioenergetics, genetics, gene expression, membrane structure, intracellular compartments, protein sorting, signaling, the cytoskeleton, the cell cycle, and apoptosis. The seventh edition incorporates advances in cryo-EM, single-molecule techniques, and genome editing.
molecular biology of the cell.note: This is a metadata summary only. Full text not included.

people we meet on vacation.title: People We Meet on Vacation
people we meet on vacation.author: Emily Henry
people we meet on vacation.summary: A contemporary romance following Alex and Poppy, best friends who take an annual vacation together for a decade. Told in alternating timelines — 'now' and 'two years ago' — the novel traces how their friendship collapsed and whether it can be rebuilt. Celebrated for its dual-timeline structure, witty banter, and emotional stakes.
people we meet on vacation.note: This is a metadata summary only. Full text not included.

seven deaths of evelyn hardcastle.title: The Seven Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle
seven deaths of evelyn hardcastle.author: Stuart Turton
seven deaths of evelyn hardcastle.summary: A mystery novel in which the protagonist relives the same day eight times, each time inhabiting a different guest at the Blackheath estate, trying to solve the murder of Evelyn Hardcastle before the day resets. The novel blends Agatha Christie-style country house mystery with a time-loop structure, exploring how perspective shapes understanding of events.
seven deaths of evelyn hardcastle.note: This is a metadata summary only. Full text not included.

the alignment problem.title: The Alignment Problem: Machine Learning and Human Values
the alignment problem.author: Brian Christian
the alignment problem.summary: A non-fiction account of the field of AI alignment — the challenge of ensuring that machine learning systems behave in accordance with human values and intentions. Christian interviews researchers across reinforcement learning, fairness, interpretability, and multi-agent systems, tracing how seemingly technical choices embed values, and what researchers are doing to address misalignment before it becomes catastrophic.

to kill a mockingbird.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
to kill a mockingbird.author: Harper Lee
to kill a mockingbird.summary: A Pulitzer Prize-winning novel set in the fictional town of Maycomb, Alabama during the 1930s, narrated by Scout Finch, a young girl whose father Atticus defends Tom Robinson, a Black man falsely accused of raping a white woman. The novel is celebrated for its moral voice, its portrayal of racial injustice in the American South, and Scout's first-person perspective as a child observer of adult hypocrisy.

visual display of quantitative informati.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information (2nd edition)
visual display of quantitative informati.author: Edward R. Tufte
visual display of quantitative informati.summary: A landmark book in data visualization arguing that well-designed statistical graphics communicate complex data efficiently and beautifully. Tufte introduces principles including data-ink ratio, chartjunk, small multiples, and sparklines. The book includes analysis of historical graphics from Minard's Napoleon campaign map to modern scientific visualizations, arguing against decorative excess and for clarity.
